input.context: Current src/urllib3/util/retry.py:342-361 parse_retry_after() only matches ^\s*[0-9]+\s*$ for delay-seconds, else falls back to HTTP-date parsing, else raises InvalidHeader. Northstar's staging upstreams send '0.5' and '+3' which hit neither branch and raise InvalidHeader today. Existing test test/test_retry.py::test_parse_retry_after_invalid explicitly asserts '+1' and '1.0' are invalid, so broadening parsing is a deliberate, narrow behavior change to this one method, not a silent one. Seeking sign-off before implementing so the change is authorized and not an unexpected retry-behavior shift. No change is proposed to retry_after_max clamping, max-sleep behavior, or to introduce any new minimum-delay/backoff floor, so this does not create retry storms beyond what Retry-After: 0 already permits today.
input.options: Accept both fractional seconds and leading '+' sign, parse as non-negative float, keep clamping to retry_after_max and rejecting negative/garbage values (closest to Northstar's two examples)|Accept fractional seconds only, keep '+3' rejected as invalid (stays closer to RFC grammar, misses one Northstar case)|Accept leading '+' sign only, keep '1.0' fractional form rejected (misses one Northstar case)|Reject both and keep current strict RFC integer-only/HTTP-date parsing (no interop change; Northstar headers continue to raise InvalidHeader)
